Forms a homooctameric ring complex; 2 8-membered rings stack back-to-back to form the hexadecameric functional complex (PubMed:12628000, PubMed:20573955, PubMed:22193720, PubMed:34362932)

Has 3 structural domains; the apical domain which binds substrate (residues 211-361), the equatorial domain (residues 1-141 and 400-543) which includes the ATP-binding and hydrolysis site and forms inter-ring contacts (via Arg-425 and Asp-451), and the intermediate domain (residues 142-210 and 362-399) which connects the other domains (PubMed:20573955). The lid region (residues 241-267) is in the apical domain; it replaces the GroES subunit of bacterial chaperonins and is required to fold a bound substrate upon ATP hydrolysis (PubMed:17460696, PubMed:20573955). The apical domain moves up to 35 A towards the equatorial domain upon ATP binding; ATP binding occurs in a random manner to at least 12/16 subunits (PubMed:34362932). The change from the open to closed conformation involves a large rotation of each subunit and changes the internal chamber volume from about 350,000-370,000 A(3) in the open state to about 130,000 A(3) in the closed state (PubMed:20573955). Closure of the chamber relies on ATP hydrolysis (PubMed:17460696)
